NOTICE OF ADVERSE DETERMINATION - MEDICAL NECESSITY

This letter constitutes an adverse determination based on medical necessity for the inpatient admission identified above. The submitted records were reviewed against the MCG-style criteria set applied by this plan for the review period in effect, and against the plan's benefit provisions.

DETERMINATION

Coverage for the inpatient admission from [[ADMIT_DATE]] through [[DISCHARGE_DATE]] is denied. The medical record does not document clinical severity sufficient to require inpatient admission.

CRITERIA REVIEWED AND FINDINGS

SEP-01: Not met. Laboratory and vital sign findings did not show sepsis with persistent instability after initial treatment.

SEP-02: Not met. An infectious source was not established.

No additional criteria were applied to this determination.

CLAIM ADJUSTMENT CODING

CARC CO-50
RARC N115

This adverse determination was made by a physician reviewer. It is an adverse determination on medical necessity grounds and is described as such throughout this notice.

APPEAL RIGHTS AND INSTRUCTIONS

A request for reconsideration may be submitted within the filing window applicable to this claim. The clinical rationale accompanying any reconsideration request must map each submitted finding to a numbered criterion as cited above. Submissions that do not correlate findings to the numbered criteria may be returned without substantive review.

Level of care denials are not eligible for provider appeal.

Appeals must be received by [[APPEAL_DEADLINE]]. Requests received after that time may be closed without further review.

Supporting documentation, including the complete medical record for the admission under review, should accompany the reconsideration request. The member or the member's authorized representative may request a copy of the specific criteria used in this determination at no charge by contacting the Utilization Management Department at the number listed on the member identification card.

This determination addresses coverage and payment only and does not direct or restrict the treatment decisions of the treating practitioner.

Sincerely,

Medical Director, Utilization Management
